title: DESIGN-LAB R5 task ledger (design-lab/task-ledger/r5-v1)
description: Contract for the live ledger design-lab/config/task-ledger-r3.json, whose schemaVersion is design-lab/task-ledger/r5-v1. The file name keeps the r3 spelling because that path is the ledger's own history: the ledger migrated r3-v1 -> r5-v1 in place on 2026-09-09 and no r5-v1 schema was written then, which is the drift this file closes. Every shape here was read off the live ledger and off the semantic rules already enforced in src/design_lab/governance/r5_contract.py: enums are the observed vocabulary, patterns are the observed ids, required lists are the observed keys, and every closed object sets additionalProperties false so a field the ledger grows without declaring it here fails. NOT expressible in JSON Schema, therefore owned by r5_contract.py and deliberately not restated as a weaker shape rule here: (1) dependency acyclicity over depends_on plus required conditional_dependencies; (2) cross-record referential integrity -- every axes.*.evidence id must exist in evidence[], evidence[].task_ids must name real tasks, and task and receipt ids must be unique; (3) equality of each task's definition/title/depends_on against the frozen taskpack docs/history/taskpacks/r5-20260908/tasks.json, and of predecessor_task_ids against the R3->R5 successor mapping; (4) required_axes derived from a task's acceptance rather than from what the ledger happens to declare; (5) axis-state coherence (implementation cannot qualify another axis, a required axis cannot be waived, a completion state requires reassessment REVIEWED); (6) the embedded predecessor must be byte-identical to the frozen r3 file and its sha256 must match; (7) RFC3339 strictness beyond format, via validate_timestamp(). The r3-v1 contract for the embedded predecessor and for docs/history/taskpacks/r3-ledger-pre-r5-20260909.json stays in task-ledger-r3.schema.json -- that file's bytes are SHA-pinned inside six evidence records, so this schema references it instead of copying it; a second copy of one contract is how the two got out of sync in the first place.

schemaVersion.description: The only version this file is the contract for. verify_ledger_schema_pairing.py selects schemas BY this value and fails hard when a version names no file -- that is exactly the branch's root cause.

taskpack.description: r5_contract.py pins this as const read from the frozen source's id; same value, so the shape and the provenance agree.

plan_path.description: r5_contract.py pins the const and separately requires the file to be readable.

baseline_sha.description: The frozen R5 source developmentSha (40 hex); r5_contract.py pins it as a const read from tasks.json.

source.description: The R5 source shape is {path, sha256}; the r3-v1 shape was {archive_sha256, tasks_sha256, body_sha256}. r5_contract.py pins the whole object as one const, so both fields are pinned here.

predecessor.description: The frozen R3 ledger this taskpack succeeded. History only through this record: it never qualifies new work (r5_contract.py).

ledger.description: The whole frozen r3 ledger, inline. Its contract is design-lab/schemas/task-ledger-r3.schema.json, which verify_ledger_schema_pairing.py applies to the file at docs/history/taskpacks/r3-ledger-pre-r5-20260909.json and separately proves this inline copy deep-equals that file; r5_contract.py pins it as a const against the same bytes. Not re-described here on purpose.

tasks.description: 28 pinned tasks, ids DL-R5-001..DL-R5-028. The inventory must also EQUAL the frozen source, which is a cross-record rule owned by r5_contract.py.

evidence.description: Append-only receipts. No maxItems on purpose: records are added by every bounded work wave, and a count pin here would be a date disguised as a contract. Uniqueness of ids and the axes -> evidence reference integrity are owned by r5_contract.py.

evidenceId.description: The naming convention all 40 live receipts follow: r5-<subject>-<YYYYMMDD>.

axisName.description: The four evidence axes; identical to the r3-v1 vocabulary and to reporting.KINDS.

hash.description: Carried over from the r3-v1 $defs.hash: a zero digest is not evidence.

timestamp.description: The same RFC3339 shape r5_contract.validate_timestamp() requires; that module additionally parses it with datetime.fromisoformat.

state.description: The r3-v1 vocabulary is unchanged in r5. Which states a given axis may hold, and that IMPLEMENTED_LOCAL on a non-implementation axis is a lie, is cross-field logic owned by r5_contract.py.

evidence.description: May be empty -- 55 of the live ledger's 112 axis records declare no evidence, the honest shape for NOT_EXECUTED/PARTIAL work. Every id here must exist in evidence[]; that is a cross-record rule owned by r5_contract.py.

taskDefinition.description: The frozen R5 taskpack delta for this task, copied verbatim from docs/history/taskpacks/r5-20260908/tasks.json; r5_contract.py rejects any edit to it by comparing against the source, so this is also a shape statement about the frozen source.

evidence_required.description: The provenance fields every R5 receipt must carry; the live vocabulary is exactly these six and appears on all 28 tasks.

axes.description: Per-axis intent as stated by the frozen taskpack. Values are const-pinned to the words all 28 frozen definitions use.

conditional_gate.description: Present on the two Comfy-gated tasks (DL-R5-008, DL-R5-024): a gate that blocks only tasks using the capability.

conditional_dependencies.description: Case-conditional edges (DL-R5-019). Whether a condition is required, and the acyclicity of the edges it adds, are decided by condition_decisions and r5_contract.py, not by shape.

depends_on.description: May be empty (DL-R5-001). Acyclicity and the existence of every named id are owned by r5_contract.py.

predecessor_task_ids.description: Historical R3 lineage only; it never qualifies new work. It must equal the R3->R5 successor mapping, which r5_contract.py checks.

reassessment.description: A completion state (PASS/IMPLEMENTED_LOCAL) on any axis requires REVIEWED; that cross-field rule is r5_contract.py's.

required_axes.description: implementation + unit always, host_live and delivery by acceptance. The set is derived from the task number by r5_contract.required_axes(), so this is a shape statement only.

condition_decisions.description: Owner decisions over a task's definition.conditional_dependencies, each with a reason. Declared because r5_contract.py accepts it and AGENTS.md requires the case-selection record; the live ledger carries none today, so this path is registered as declared-but-unused in verify_ledger_schema_pairing.py and must leave that register the moment a ledger uses it.

artifact.description: Same item shape as the r3-v1 schema's artifacts. Existence and digest truth are checked elsewhere -- verify_evidence_artifact_presence.py and reporting.project_ledger().

kind.description: Which kind may support which axis is reporting.KINDS, not a shape rule.

binding.description: WORKTREE_FILES says the bytes came from a dirty tree and may never be presented as a commit.

software.description: What produced the observation. Keys are open on purpose -- the live ledger already uses 18 distinct names (python, os, runner, node, host, torch, gh, git, observation, review, platform, test_manifest, worktree_digest, typecheck, full_suite, clean_install, typescript, vite) and a closed list would block an honest new measurement rather than a false one. Values stay non-empty strings so a version cannot arrive as a nested claim.

subject_files.description: {repository-relative POSIX path: sha256 of the bytes observed}. Required non-empty because this is the only part of a receipt a stranger can recompute -- see verify_ledger_subject_binding.py. Path safety (no drive letters, no escapes, declared public roots) is enforced by reporting._safe(), not by pattern.

artifacts.description: Documents the receipt produced. An empty list was one of the two defects that froze the projections; the r3-v1 schema already required one.
